introText:
The Hult Prize is the world's largest student startup competition — a year-long journey that takes a team from a single idea to a shot at $1,000,000 USD in seed funding. Every venture has to be for-profit and has to support at least one UN Sustainable Development Goal. This year's theme, "Unlimited," means teams can build toward any SDG they choose, rather than a single assigned theme.

Below is the real path a team follows from our own OnCampus competition all the way to the Global Finals, how judges actually score teams at each stage, and the Sustainable Development Goals a venture can be built around.

stages.name: Qualifiers
stages.description: Teams compete through their campus's own Hult Prize OnCampus program — like the one our chapter runs — or, if no local competition is available to them, through Hult Prize's Open Application process instead.

stages.name: Nationals
stages.description: Teams that qualify move on to national or regional competition events, or an equivalent online selection process, where they compete against qualifiers from other campuses.

stages.name: Digital Incubator
stages.description: Selected teams enter a structured mentorship program: refining the core idea, validating real product-market fit, and building an actual minimum viable product.

stages.name: Global Accelerator
stages.description: An intensive, in-person program at Ashridge House in London — compressing months of normal startup development into a few high-pressure weeks alongside teams from around the world.

stages.name: Global Finals
stages.description: The remaining teams pitch live for the $1,000,000 USD prize in front of judges, marking the end of the yearly competition cycle.

eligibility: Every team member must be at least 18 years old
Every team member must be enrolled in any degree-granting program (undergraduate or graduate)
The venture must be for-profit, not a nonprofit or charity
The venture must support at least one UN Sustainable Development Goal — this year's theme, "Unlimited," means any SDG qualifies, not one assigned theme

evaluationCriteria.name: Innovation & Impact
evaluationCriteria.description: How original the idea is, and how much real-world scale and impact it could realistically reach if it worked.

evaluationCriteria.name: Business Model Viability
evaluationCriteria.description: Whether the venture can actually sustain itself financially — real revenue thinking, not just a good cause.

evaluationCriteria.name: Execution & Traction
evaluationCriteria.description: Real, demonstrated progress: working prototypes, actual user engagement, evidence the team has already started building, not just planning.

evaluationCriteria.name: Team Strength & Leadership
evaluationCriteria.description: How committed and organized the team is, and how well its members' skills and backgrounds complement each other.

sdgs.name: No Poverty
sdgs.description: Ending poverty in all its forms, everywhere.

sdgs.name: Zero Hunger
sdgs.description: Ending hunger, achieving food security, and promoting sustainable agriculture.
sdgs.example: Illustrative example only — not a real venture: a platform connecting surplus restaurant and grocery food to local food banks.

sdgs.name: Good Health and Well-being
sdgs.description: Ensuring healthy lives and promoting well-being for people at every age.

sdgs.name: Quality Education
sdgs.description: Ensuring inclusive, equitable, quality education and lifelong learning opportunities for all.

sdgs.name: Gender Equality
sdgs.description: Achieving gender equality and empowering all women and girls.

sdgs.name: Clean Water and Sanitation
sdgs.description: Ensuring availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all.
sdgs.example: Illustrative example only — not a real venture: a low-cost, community-maintained water filtration system for underserved regions.

sdgs.name: Affordable and Clean Energy
sdgs.description: Ensuring access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy for all.
sdgs.example: Illustrative example only — not a real venture: pay-as-you-go solar charging kiosks for off-grid communities.

sdgs.name: Decent Work and Economic Growth
sdgs.description: Promoting sustained, inclusive economic growth and decent work for all.
sdgs.example: Illustrative example only — not a real venture: a micro-lending platform for informal-sector workers.

sdgs.name: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure
sdgs.description: Building resilient infrastructure and fostering innovation.

sdgs.name: Reduced Inequalities
sdgs.description: Reducing inequality within and among countries.

sdgs.name: Sustainable Cities and Communities
sdgs.description: Making cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient, and sustainable.

sdgs.name: Responsible Consumption and Production
sdgs.description: Ensuring sustainable consumption and production patterns.
sdgs.example: Illustrative example only — not a real venture: a marketplace for upcycled and refurbished electronics.

sdgs.name: Climate Action
sdgs.description: Taking urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts.
sdgs.example: Illustrative example only — not a real venture: a carbon-footprint tracking subscription for small businesses.

sdgs.name: Life Below Water
sdgs.description: Conserving and sustainably using the oceans, seas, and marine resources.

sdgs.name: Life on Land
sdgs.description: Protecting, restoring, and promoting sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems.

sdgs.name: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
sdgs.description: Promoting peaceful, inclusive societies and building effective, accountable institutions.

sdgs.name: Partnerships for the Goals
sdgs.description: Strengthening global partnerships to support and achieve all of the goals together.
